claims: Resistance exercise selection requires qualified instruction, safe equipment and space, appropriate progression, and readiness assessed for the individual rather than inferred from an exercise label.

Before {{canonicalName}}, check the support or anchor, hand position, clearance, mount, exit, traffic, symptoms, and fatigue. Training should be individualized and progressively developed from current readiness and movement competence.

Scale {{canonicalName}} with stable support height or a lower bar, neutral-grip handles, a shorter lever, reduced leg height, shorter holds, more rest, safe assistance, plain-language cues, visual timing, or a supported or supine substitute. assessmentSummary.identity: A static bilateral compression exercise performed in straight-arm push support on the floor, parallettes, boxes, dip bars, parallel bars, or rings. The athlete presses into the support while holding the declared leg shape and height in front. Knee angle, leg position, support height, assistance, hold time, and implement stability are controlled variant or delivery dimensions.
currentCardFindings: The historical Tuck L-Sit Hold is a short-lever variant of L-Sit, not a separate stable identity.

One-leg, full legs-together, straddle, and ring-support versions preserve static straight-arm support compression but materially change lever, symmetry, flexibility, stability, difficulty, supervision, and dosage.
Support height, heel taps, foot assistance, hold time, range, and rest are modifier or delivery annotations when the support action and intended hold remain unchanged.
Hanging L-Sit changes straight-arm push support to overhead suspension, introducing different shoulder, grip, anchor, mount, and exit demands; it is a separate exercise definition.
V-sit and Manna change the required leg height, shoulder relationship, and principal training demand enough to require separate exercise definitions and review.
The former generic 40/20/40 scores understated straight-arm support, shoulder depression and protraction, compression, long-lever knee extension, breathing, and exit demands.
Exercise difficulty is assessed only as exercise complexity and physical difficulty, with overall equal to their maximum. This exercise card carries no athlete or class level.
